# First release

<!-- Generated by node scripts/contract-docs.mjs write from CONTRACT.md. -->

The acceptance journeys and implementation evidence below come from [CONTRACT.md](CONTRACT.md). Its complete clause text remains authoritative. Status describes current implementation, not a reduced target.

## Workspace and HTTP delivery

- **WORK-001 — Visual multi-step workspace. Status: partial.** From the builder, connect a new lead trigger to a filter, CRM lookup, invoice draft and notification; test the trigger to load recent real leads from the connected test account and pick one, test each step and inspect the sample data and its named source at every edge, correct a missing required field, save and reopen the same graph, then publish it deliberately and observe its next triggered run complete with no further authorization step.
  Current evidence: `src/crank/ui/flows.ts`; `src/crank/flows.ts`; `tests/crank.test.mjs`; `src/crank/workflows/store.ts`; `src/crank/engine/graph.ts` Remaining: No visual node-and-edge editor, no sample data on edges (WORK-014), no picker-filled steps (CONN-019).

## Build the automation

- **WORK-002 — Mapping, formatting and conditional routes. Status: partial.** Use the builder with a US lead containing nested addresses, a missing optional field and a USD amount; test both qualifying and filtered branches, a null value and invalid currency input, then inspect the exact mapped destination payload. Map a HubSpot deal with 3 line items (one discounted, one non-taxable) and a Square order with 4 lines into QuickBooks Online sandbox draft invoices: readback shows 3 and 4 lines with matching quantities, amounts and tax codes, and each invoice total equals its source total to the cent; build a 2-line invoice with a line-itemizer step from comma-separated sheet values; zip parallel lists of unequal length and verify a named error; send a zero-line source and verify a named validation failure and no invoice created. Map a Typeform file-upload URL into a Google Drive upload and verify the file by readback with its name, type and size; map a URL that redirects to a private-network address and verify `file fetch failed` with no request past the refusal and no write.
  Current evidence: `src/crank/engine/mapping.ts`; `src/crank/engine/transforms/index.ts`; `src/crank/connectors/files.ts`; `tests/logic.test.mjs`; `tests/connections.test.mjs` Remaining: Connector schema validation; HubSpot, Square and QuickBooks line-item read&#47;write and Drive upload readback need accounts (HubSpot, Square, QuickBooks sandbox, Typeform, Google Drive).

- **WORK-003 — Loops, joins and batch processing. Status: done.** Run a paginated order batch through a loop and two branches, join by order ID, interrupt after some invoices are created and resume; inspect unmatched records and confirm each completed order retains one invoice.
  Current evidence: `src/crank/engine/loop.ts`; `src/crank/engine/graph.ts`; `src/crank/engine/executor.ts`; `src/crank/engine/steps/join.ts`; `src/crank/connectors/pagination.ts`; `tests/batch.test.mjs`; `tests/pagination.test.mjs` (WORK-003)

- **WORK-004 — Durable delay and event waits. Status: done.** Publish a two-business-day follow-up, stop the executor while waiting, resume after a timezone&#47;DST boundary and deliver the same callback twice; observe one continuation, or the configured timeout branch if the deadline passes. Send 5 runs from two workflows into one named delay queue with 1-minute spacing and restart the service mid-queue; verify each releases once, in arrival order, at least 60 seconds after the previous. While work is queued, declare that queue from a second workflow with different spacing; verify visible refusal at declaration and that the queued work, spacing, order and release times are unchanged. Verify the second workflow can share the queue with the same spacing or use a distinct queue name without accelerating the existing queued work.
  Current evidence: `src/crank/engine/steps/flow.ts`; `src/crank/engine/records.ts`; `src/crank/ops/delay-queues.ts`; `src/crank/ops/scheduler.ts`; `src/crank/triggers/callbacks.ts`; `tests/logic.test.mjs` (WORK-004: storage interruption, concurrent release, restart, DST, expiry and cancellation)

- **WORK-005 — Isolated code steps and external executors. Declare a nested output schema: reject malformed&#47;unsupported declarations, pass matching values without coercion, stop mismatched results before downstream effects and validate the same task under the immutable schema after restart. Current structural schema semantics and bounds are documented in docs/API.md; other WORK-005 obligations remain in scope.

Make the provider return 500 during a search and verify a failure, not `not found`; map an empty email as the key and verify a named validation error and no search. Repeat the halt and continue settings on a WORK-007 table lookup and a CONN-011 custom connector search with the same outcomes. Migrate a Zap whose HubSpot search uses “create if it doesn’t exist” and verify the coverage report calls it native and its parity test passes.

## Connections and triggers

- **CONN-001 — Discoverable connector library. Status: partial.** Find a CRM connector by a business action, connect a test account, discover custom fields and see them load as mappable step inputs through a CONN-019 picker, test a paginated lookup and inspect the exact action scope and unsupported-operation message before publishing. Feed the coverage report a 60-Zap SMB inventory built only from Zapier’s 22 popular apps, using a fixed operation list committed with the test: for each app, every trigger, search and action used by that app’s ten most-used Zapier templates as captured on 16 October 2026, plus the built-in tools mapped above (including RSS, Retrieve Poll, Digest, Line-itemizer, every Formatter transform those templates use, every filter and path rule operator and fallback they use, every chosen account resource, and every search with “create if it doesn’t exist” or a no-match or multiple-result setting): every app, operation and setting reports native. Add three long-tail apps (one with a public OpenAPI description, one with documented REST but no OpenAPI, one with a partner-only API) and verify agent-buildable, agent-buildable and blocked-with-reason respectively. Feed a second inventory of accounting Zaps using every QuickBooks Online and Xero trigger, search and action CONN-007 names, plus one QuickBooks operation it does not name: verify the named operations report native and the unnamed one reports agent-buildable. Feed a third inventory of commerce and support Zaps using every Shopify and Stripe trigger, search and action CONN-008 names and every Zendesk and Jira Software Cloud trigger, search and action CONN-009 names, plus one Shopify and one Zendesk operation those clauses do not name: verify every named operation reports native and the two unnamed ones report agent-buildable. Feed a fourth inventory of AI Zaps using every ChatGPT (OpenAI), Anthropic (Claude) and AI by Zapier action and search mapped above, with text, PDF, image, audio and URL inputs: verify every step reports native with its AI-001 operation named, and that an OpenAI action this clause does not map reports agent-buildable.
  Current evidence: `src/crank/connections/catalog.ts`; `src/crank/ops/coverage.ts`; `tests/connections.test.mjs` Remaining: Breadth: of Zapier's 22 popular apps only Slack is native; Zapier JSON export format; custom-field discovery.

- **CONN-007 — QuickBooks Online, Xero and NetSuite. Status: missing.** For each provider’s sandbox, map a customer and a source with five lines (mixed tax codes, one discount line and one non-taxable line) into a draft invoice, read it back with five lines whose per-line amounts and total match the source to the cent, handle a locked period and revoked scope, and record a payment reference without rounding cents away. Then, in a QuickBooks Online sandbox: 1. Moving a HubSpot deal to Closed Won runs **find or create customer** by email; run it twice for one new customer and verify `created`, then `found`, and one customer by readback. 2. Create a final 3-line invoice for that customer and **send** it: readback shows the invoice’s email status as sent, and the sandbox inbox receives it. Lose the send response and retry: the inbox receives one email. 3. A Stripe test-mode charge **records a payment** applied to that invoice: readback shows a zero balance and the invoice as paid. - **CONN-010 — Every Run Edit Run product connects. Status: partial.** For each listed sibling, connect an authorized installation, receive a real domain event, read the originating record, perform an allowed domain action and observe its outcome in that sibling; duplicate events, revoked grants and foreign-tenant IDs must fail safely. Demonstrate a CRM-to-accounting-to-chat business journey across sibling connectors. **Delivered native slice:** Nook's documented integration-token action posts a body to one immutable HTTPS installation and conversation binding. Existing native-owner connection management, publication, test-account controls, current request admission and audit apply. Each physical request rechecks current connection and messages:write authority. A stable operation key uses Nook's family-scoped provider idempotency contract. Lost acknowledgements retry within the retained bounded budget only with the original credential; replacing its bearer leaves a possibly accepted operation uncertain because the posting API cannot attest family continuity. Resealing the same credential is safe. Definite 401 and 403 refusals can re-execute after explicit owner reconnect and resume, while prior possibly accepted writes retain their credential fence. Long provider waits park across restart. A provider response is labelled an acknowledgement, never independent readback. Destination refusal also applies when the credential is used through the generic HTTP door. Connection bindings and completed history restore without credentials, receiving authority or automatic execution. Named edge assertions are in `tests/nook-journey.mjs`, invoked by `tests/connections.test.mjs`; existing owned-operation conformance includes this action. `tests/sibling-browser.mjs` is invoked by Verify. This is partial delivery of the unchanged acceptance above; no real sibling event, record lookup or cross-product completion is established.
  Current evidence: `tests/connections.test.mjs` — Native Nook delivery binds installation and conversation, retains one effect across lost acknowledgements and fences current authority; `tests/ownership.test.mjs` — BASE-001&#47;BASE-004 owned installation; `tests/sibling-browser.mjs` — native Nook recovery, uncertainty, editor text and tooltips, acknowledgement and revoked screens. Remaining: Only the Nook integration-token send action is delivered, with edge proof; no authorized live sibling receipt. Domain events, originating-record lookups, independent readback, the other listed siblings and the CRM-to-accounting-to-chat journey remain unproved. Orbit API-001 lacks general public credentials and outbound subscriptions; Nook lacks events and message-history access. These require sibling-owned public doors. Changed bearer continuity after a possibly accepted write remains unverified, including provider rotations that preserve the family; Crank keeps that work uncertain rather than replaying it.

- **CONN-011 — Custom, enterprise and private app connections: custom connectors, private gateways and pipelines. Status: done.** Install a custom connector, call a private test database through an enrolled gateway, checkpoint and resume a paginated file pipeline, then revoke the gateway and attempt a cross-environment secret read; inspect the failed run and access decisions. Verify an expired or reused enrollment code and a gateway request with a wrong signature or environment are refused, an operation or destination outside the grant and a new connector version without a grant are refused at Crank and at the gateway, and the database credential is absent from Crank state, run history, logs and archives. Run each named recipe (PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, SFTP and S3-compatible) against a real test server through the gateway, and verify a scoped service account is refused outside its environment and scopes. Current gateway semantics follow ct’s 21 October ruling. TEAM-001 authority revision changes on enrollment, gateway&#47;grant changes and member authority changes. SEC-003 audits code lifecycle, grants, revocations and refused dispatches without credentials or payloads. DATA-001&#47;DATA-002 restore gateway metadata revoked and grants inactive with no code, gateway key or authority. BASE-003 reports gateway last seen, program version and status. TEAM-003 service accounts inherit the environment, expiry and minter-authority boundary. WORK-011 custom searches use this clause; AGENT-002 repairs need a new exact-version grant. Agent-buildable coverage in AI-001, MIG-001–003 and CONN-001 belongs to CONN-020. Public custom connector DNS enforcement remains SEC-002’s own Base egress gap, as ct ruled; private gateways perform their own checked resolution.
  Current evidence: `tests/connections.test.mjs` — “Custom connector review, agent OpenAPI proposal and sandbox gates retain exact versions, scope refusals and signed duplicate-event proof” (install, typed scopes, immutable versions and sandbox); “Enrolled private gateway reads a real database, checkpoints file pages across restart, revokes dispatch and restores without gateway authority” (database&#47;file resume, signed identity, code reuse, dual grants, cross-environment decisions, host custody and inactive restore); “Private gateway read retries retain admission, inputs and budget across restart, recover automatically and stop at exhaustion”. `tests/service-accounts.test.mjs` — “CONN-011 / TEAM-003: owner email confirmation mints hash-only expiring preparation accounts with explicit doors and scoped reads”; “CONN-011 / TEAM-003: scope moves, expiry and minter changes permanently suspend accounts and fence admitted draft commits”. `tests/postgres-write-journey.mjs` — real restricted PostgreSQL write, owner confirmation, independent business readback, lost-result receipt recovery and timeout uncertainty. `tests/custom-browser.mjs` with `tests/private-write-browser.mjs` — native Connections, Access, editor and run end states at 1440/390, including an actual PostgreSQL write. `tests/database-gateway-journey.mjs` — real PostgreSQL&#47;MySQL restricted reads, typed inputs, bounds and session cleanup; `tests/sqlserver-gateway-journey.mjs` — real SQL Server restricted login&#47;READ_ONLY database, exact grants, byte/row/deadline limits, session cleanup and refusal; `tests/storage-provider-journey.mjs` — real OpenSSH SFTP&#47;RustFS S3 pages, restart, source&#47;credential refusal and custody; `tests/storage-gateway-journey.mjs` — network-edge redirect, UTF-8 and protocol bounds; `tests/gateway-streaming-journey.mjs` — real 64 MiB source, 64 KiB pages, restart and same-size mutation refusal. `tests/retry-backoff-journey.mjs` — “Real owner email freshness, expired enrollment and 90-second Retry-After plus 1/2/4/8/16-minute public and private outage backoff survive restart” (actual five-minute step-up, expired fifteen-minute code, native/public/private bounded backoff, retained input and budget, first due Cron and automatic recovery).

## Connections and triggers

## Operate recurring work

- **EXEC-001 — Durable queues and execution checkpoints. ## Approvals and data custody

- **TEAM-002 — Optional approvals and standing grants. Status: done.** Publish a routine lead workflow with no grant and observe unattended completion; give an agent task a limited grant and observe it complete within the grant; exceed a USD refund limit, inspect and reject one proposed action, approve another, then alter its body and revoke the grant mid-run, verifying reapproval&#47;refusal and recorded in-flight uncertainty. **Delivered semantics (ct ruling, 20 October 2026 11:50Z):** The native owner issues a separate, one-time-shown, hash-held execution credential bound to an immutable grant and the issuing owner's current identity&#47;version; preparation credentials remain preparation-only. The owner chooses the workflow&#47;version, each existing leaf tool and app&#47;account, allowed top-level input fields (including their JSON subtrees), exact recipient paths&#47;values, nonnegative USD amounts, per-tool rolling-minute admission limits, UTC expiry, native delegates and timeout&#47;escalation recipients. Agents choose and order a subset of the declared tools, at most once per task, with literal inputs; transport, connections, retry&#47;readback settings and source policy remain owner-declared. Each task retains an immutable graph and the source workflow's full owner-estimated per-run cost reservation; submitted values use the existing sealed&#47;erasable run payload. USD bounds are inclusive exact decimal comparisons without rounding; the rate window is the preceding 60 seconds, one admission per tool invocation, with retries retaining that admission. Above-limit effects wait for a human decision on their exact input. A changed held proposal, including a deferred approved proposal, clears the old decision and retains the input revision and decision audit; no dispatched effect can be revised. The owner selects native delegates; after the owner-chosen timeout, a durable internal Approvals task opens to the escalation recipients without automatic approval or an external-delivery claim. Every step and physical request checks live grant/version/connection authority. Revocation fences leases and records already-started writes as uncertain, never as cancelled remote effects. Grants and rate authority stay installation-local; portable task graphs, payloads, decisions, escalation history and audit restore inactive. Explicit receiving-owner adoption at publish can authorize a frozen task as fixed native work, retaining source-grant provenance in its immutable declaration&#47;audit; the source execution credential remains inert and new agent tasks need a fresh grant. Current conformance covers every existing tool; added tools&#47;doors under WORK-005/006/007/009/010/011/014, CONN-003 through CONN-019, EXEC-007, AI-001/002/003, AGENT-001/002/003/004 and PLATFORM-001/002 inherit the same grant, exact-review, revocation, custody and recovery obligations before shipping. Before shipping AI-003, pin both versions, adopt a new version and verify next-run-only use and frozen open runs; refuse widened authority until the owner issues the required grant. Revoke a tool before the next step dispatch and verify refusal. Require a human decision for a new version's first external send unless a standing grant covers it, and deny agent approval. Verify the grant cannot bypass configured cadence, invoice billing-contact-only recipients, the same-dispatch connected-invoice read, operation-key deduplication or any AI-003 stop (paid/closed/void, takeover, cancellation, owner pause, expiry or budget hold).
  Current evidence: `src/crank/grants/store.ts`; `src/crank/grants/authority.ts`; `src/crank/grants/policy.ts`; `src/crank/grants/tasks.ts`; `src/crank/grants/proposals.ts`; `src/crank/grants/reviews.ts`; `src/crank/engine/executor.ts`; `src/crank/ui/grants.ts`; `migrations/core/0047_standing_grants.sql`; `tests/grants.test.mjs`; `tests/grants-browser.mjs` (TEAM-002: grant-free execution, bounded agent tasks, exact edits&#47;review, changed input, delegation&#47;deadline, rate, revocation uncertainty and inactive restore)

## AI steps

- **AI-001 — Inspectable AI and agent nodes. Status: missing.** Run an invoice-extraction node on the installation’s default model with no model key configured and see its USD usage in OPS-002, then run a tool-using agent on a buyer-selected endpoint against authorized documents and MCP tools; inspect model/tool/cost provenance, inject a hostile instruction and exceed a tool&#47;spend limit, verifying schema failure or escalation without an unauthorized write. An extract-structured-data node reads the PDF as a file reference, not as pasted text, and returns vendor, bill number, date, three line items and total. A QuickBooks Online sandbox bill is created for the vendor, found or created by name (CONN-007), with the PDF attached. Readback shows lines and total matching the PDF to the cent. 2. **Receipt photo.** Send a JPEG receipt photo by Twilio MMS (CONN-017). An analyze node extracts merchant, date and total into a Google Sheets row, verified by readback. 3. **Transcription.** Deliver a Zoom test recording-completed event (CONN-013) with a 3-minute two-speaker recording. A transcribe node returns text with timestamps; a send-prompt node lists the action items, and one Asana task per action item is created (CONN-014), verified by readback. 4. **URL extraction.** An extract-content-from-URL node reads a public test page and a public PDF into text. Send audio to the same node through an untyped file input at run time: the step fails with `model input unsupported` and makes no write. 6. **Default model.** Run steps 1 and 3 on the installation’s default model with no model key configured, and see each run’s USD usage in OPS-002.
